title: AAWSAP and BAASS, 2007-2012
notes: Start-here flag 1; the lineage thread starts here.

lead.text: AAWSAP was a Defense Intelligence Agency programme, paid for with $22 million appropriated at Senator Harry Reid's direction, under which Robert Bigelow's company BAASS, the only bidder, studied far-term foreign aerospace threats from 2008. The Department's own 2024 history confirms that the contractor also conducted UFO research and investigated a Utah ranch owned by its head.

summary.text: DIA records that Reid and Senator Inouye sponsored a $10 million add in the FY2008 supplemental appropriation to investigate foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats out 40 years and to build a centre of expertise, and that the FY2010 Defense Appropriations Act added $12 million more.

DIA posted solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 on 18 August 2008, naming James Lacatski as Government Project Leader and aiming to understand the physics and engineering of these applications through 2050. It drew one bid, from Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, and contract HHM402-08-C-0072 was signed on 22 September 2008 at a $10 million base with four option years.

BAASS commissioned and delivered the technical reports known as the Defense Intelligence Reference Documents, 26 in FY2009 and 12 in FY2010. In June 2009 Reid asked the Deputy Secretary of Defense to make parts of the programme a restricted special access programme; DIA and the Under Secretary for Intelligence recommended against it and the request was refused.
AARO's history says the programme was terminated in 2012, and that its supporters then proposed a successor, KONA BLUE, to the Department of Homeland Security.

record.text: The solicitation was coded as special studies and analysis rather than research and development, set aside for small business, and issued by DIA's Virginia Contracting Activity, with one firm fixed price contract anticipated.

A USD(I) memorandum to the Deputy Secretary states that the AAITP Reid refers to is officially the AAWSAP contract managed by DIA, that its primary purpose is to investigate revolutionary advances in future aerospace technologies, and that the resulting contract was for unclassified research in 11 technical areas to be reported by 31 July 2009.

DIA's own briefings rate BAASS's performance as excellent: 12 project management plans, 26 research reports by 30 June 2009 (twice the minimum), and reviews that were overwhelmingly positive. They recommend exercising option year 1, record a satisfactory Defense Security Service inspection of the BAASS facility on 17 December 2008, and state that SCI clearances were completed for all key personnel.

DIA's review memo of 30 October 2009 records thirteen reviews of the 26 FY2009 reports, eight by other report authors and five by outside reviewers, three of them Sandia staff. All the reviews were positive, some exceptionally so, and the programme manager reviewed every paper and concurred.

The contract's FY2010 option was exercised on 2 September 2009. Every key government name in the released contract is redacted, and DIA withheld the contract in a 2011 FOIA response, releasing it only in October 2022.

Reid's letter of 24 June 2009, on Majority Leader letterhead to Deputy Secretary William Lynn, asks for a restricted special access programme with a bigoted access list for specific portions of the effort, including methods for engineering advanced technologies and the involvement of private contractors, projected from FY09 to FY13. The Department's spokesperson authenticated it in June 2019.

DIA papers document Reid meeting DIA leadership on the programme at least four times, on 13 November 2008, 5 January 2009, in mid-May 2009 and on 19 November 2009 in the Senate Visitor Center with the Deputy Secretary present, the last to address his special access request and the quality of the products.

DIA's memo of 13 November 2009 found insufficient grounds to classify the open programme or make it a restricted special access programme, said the information was not owned by or under the control of the government, and that DIA may not classify basic scientific research. It says FY2009 deliverables were unclassified because the contractor had no secure facility yet, and that four to six reports would be expanded with classified data in FY2010.

The 17 November 2009 decision packet for the Deputy Secretary records Clapper, as USD(I), recommending against a special access programme at that time, and DIA's October 2009 technical reviews of 26 papers finding no justification for one.

Lacatski is named as Government Project Leader on the public solicitation, the only unredacted appearance of the programme manager, and redacted in every later release. DIA found no records of the 19 June 2007 letter to Bigelow that his book describes.

AARO's Volume I confirms the $22 million at Reid's direction, that DIA established AAWSAP in 2009, and that the contractor conducted UFO research with the DIA programme manager's support although UAP investigation was not in the statement of work, including at a Utah property then owned by the head of the contractor.

Bigelow founded NIDS in 1995 as a privately funded institute studying aerial phenomena and animal mutilations, and bought the Utah ranch in 1996, owning it throughout the DIA contract. The contract was held by BAASS, an LLC with its own DUNS and CAGE codes, separate from Bigelow Aerospace.
The New York Times revealed the programme on 16 December 2017, reporting that most of the money went to Bigelow Aerospace; Reid told the paper he was not embarrassed or sorry he got it going.

claimed.text: By the account of Lacatski, Kelleher and Knapp in their book, the programme began when Lacatski read Kelleher and Knapp's Hunt for the Skinwalker, wrote to Bigelow on DIA letterhead in June 2007, visited the ranch and reported an experience there, which Bigelow relayed to Reid. This origin story rests on the co-authors' own account; DIA reports no record of the letter.
Knapp is credited with introducing Reid to Bigelow, and reporting has Reid, Inouye and Stevens directing the money into the classified budget together in 2007.

Lacatski told Jeremy Corbell in 2026 that the programme built the world's largest UFO data warehouse and more than 100 detailed reports, and that he doubts the files will ever be released. Knapp testified that BAASS recruited about 50 cleared investigators over 27 months and built a 240,000-case data warehouse designed by Jacques Vallee.

Kelleher, deputy administrator of BAASS after leading the NIDS ranch team, is said to have run the contract day to day, with parallel physics and human biological effects programmes. A leaked 494-page BAASS Ten Month Report of July 2009 describes field investigation, case database work and ranch operations.
Reporting has BAASS funding MUFON's Star Team rapid-response project in 2009 and 2010, and sending teams to Brazil in 2009 to study the Colares case wave for its DIA sponsor.

Knapp testified under oath in September 2025 that Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with Lockheed Martin executives for material held at a California facility, and named Lockheed as one holder; Elizondo told the House in November 2024 that the transfer was blocked.
Bigelow told 60 Minutes in 2017 that he is absolutely convinced of an extraterrestrial presence on Earth.

contested.text: AARO says the programme ended in 2012 due to DIA and DoD concerns, and its account of KONA BLUE says DIA cancelled it for lack of merit; DIA's 2009 review found every review positive. The board infers that the merit judgement was applied after the fact for institutional reasons.
DIA's refusal of special access status evaluated only the written deliverables, never the field investigation, database or human-effects work the same contract paid for.

The board infers that the requirement was written to fit BAASS: a five-week competition on a statement of work including spatial and temporal translation and human effects, awarded to the one firm with a decade of that field practice, through a contracting office largely absent from public award data.

AARO confirms the Utah investigation, but DIA says it cannot locate the ranch investigation report its authors describe, which the board reads as the field record being held by the contractor or never filed.

The records pull in different directions on who managed the programme: the board's note on Lacatski says his identification as the redacted programme manager rested on his own accounts and secondary reporting, while one released copy of the Davis wormholes paper names James T. Lacatski as AAWSA Program Manager.

The records disagree on details: the solicitation and the USD(I) memo describe 11 technical areas where a DIA talking paper lists twelve; the contract modification gives BAASS a North Las Vegas address where the award gives a Las Vegas one; and Reid's request is dated 24 June 2009 in DIA's release but 24 July 2009 in the memorandum the spokesperson authenticated.

On the board's reading, a bigoted access list over a programme whose deliverables were unclassified literature reviews suggests Reid was protecting something not represented in them, and routing the money through the classified annex kept the authorising committees from seeing it.

AARO says executives of the companies named by interviewees denied the programmes on the record, without naming any company or describing any inspection, against Knapp's and Elizondo's account of a Lockheed transfer.

questions: What did Lacatski's June 2007 letter to Bigelow say, and why does DIA have no record of it?
Where are the BAASS Ten Month Report, the monthly reports and the ranch investigation report now, and who holds them?
Did BAASS ever transfer physical samples to DIA, and under what receipt?
How many people did BAASS employ, and has NIDS's raw field data ever been examined independently?
Into which appropriations account was the $22 million placed, and how much was obligated in each option year?
What happened to the four to six reports DIA said would be expanded with classified data in FY2010?
Was any material ever physically delivered to Bigelow Aerospace, and what is the California facility?
